title: ONE BYTE CHANGES. VERIFY NAMES IT.
question: What does a saved bundle detect when a referenced file changes later?
takeaway: A saved fingerprint and a later fingerprint differ, so verify reports the referenced file mismatch instead of hiding the change.

reading_speeds.at_20_seconds: Bundle records result.json at baseline time; verify with run root re-hashes it later and names the mismatch.
reading_speeds.at_2_minutes: The exact error and digest examples come from one render manifest, while adjacent prose preserves the limits of an unsigned retrospective baseline.

medium.rationale: The before/after fingerprints and exact mismatch text require deterministic, shared desktop/mobile semantics.

labels.claim: Bundle records the selected file fingerprint at baseline time.
The referenced file may later contain different bytes.
Verify with run root re-hashes the current referenced file.
The expected digest comes from the saved bundle.
The actual digest is computed from current local bytes.
A referenced-file digest mismatch fails verification with exit one.

labels.text: Referenced file digest mismatch for result.json
labels.claim: The report names the changed reference.

boundaries: The bundle must be retained separately from the source files to serve as a later baseline.
Anyone who edits an unsigned bundle can recompute its embedded digest.
A mismatch detects changed bytes; it does not identify an actor or determine which value is true.

accessibility.alt_text: A saved result.json fingerprint differs from its later fingerprint, so verify reports a referenced-file digest mismatch and exits one.
accessibility.long_description: A compact three-step line reads Save, Change, Verify. Save records result.json with reward one and digest 8d14 through a6c2. Change shows reward zero and digest f913 through 7b40. Verify compares expected and actual fingerprints, displays a not-equal sign, and reports the named result.json mismatch with exit one.
